questions.question: For routine braking, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar can:

options.text: Tip over if you turn too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tip over if you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast for the corner.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Practice riding on a quiet road first to get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight of a passenger or load.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and keep a safe space cushion.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before starting to pass.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.
Hope that another driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope that another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure you are visible and other drivers know your plans. Signal clearly and position your lane well. Maintain a safe space and watch ahead for hazards.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Gently brake using the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake using the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and stay straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Usually, the best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by making them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes together firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock up.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Only use your mirrors to check your surroundings.
Point in the direction you plan to change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: It only matters if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a crash. Using too much rear brake locks the rear wheel. When the rear wheel locks, you lose the ability to turn. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for at least one hour
After riding for more than 8 hours

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than 5 miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across.
Hold tight to the grips and speed up to get past the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Just stay calm and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: How should a passenger sit and move on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as the operator leans
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean the same way they lean. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact
Never assume other drivers see you
Focus only on moving through the intersection
Speed up so others notice you

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still fail to notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: The body gets rid of about one drink per hour. A person drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours. How many drinks are likely still in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To estimate how many drinks remain, subtract the hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. In this example: 7 drinks consumed minus 3 hours = 4 drinks remaining in the system.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Use only your mirrors to check for other vehicles
Turn your head to look for traffic behind you
Do not worry about other traffic
Brake hard to let vehicles in your blind spot pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic behind you
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: How do you stop in the shortest distance in a straight line?

options.text: Use both brakes without locking either wheel
Use both brakes while locking the rear wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel
questions.explanation: Use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance on a straight road. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers
Make it easier for others to see you

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, keeps you out of blind spots, avoids road hazards, shows your intentions, reduces wind blasts from other vehicles, and gives you an escape route. It should not help you avoid being seen.
